one_line_description.value: Apify is the largest marketplace of tools for AI, with ready-made Actors to automate business workflows.
one_line_description.quote: Apify is the largest marketplace of tools for AI.

has_public_api.quote: The Apify API (version 2) provides programmatic access to the Apify platform.

api_type.quote: The Apify API is built around HTTP REST, uses predictable resource-oriented URLs, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.

api_breadth.value: Broad read-write REST surface: Actors, runs, builds, tasks, datasets, key-value stores, request queues, schedules, webhooks, users/account
api_breadth.quote: Apify API documentation: Endpoints to manage Actors, runs, builds, tasks, datasets, key-value stores, request queues, schedules, webhooks, and your account.

docs_url.quote: The Apify API (version 2) provides programmatic access to the Apify platform.

auth_methods.quote: You can authenticate the Apify API in two ways. You can either pass the token via the `Authorization` HTTP header or the URL `token` query parameter.

access_model.quote: The best way to find the costs of free Actors upfront is to try out the Actor on a limited scope (for example, on a small number of pages) and evaluate the consumption. You can easily do that using our free plan.

access_notes.value: Self-serve: sign up free and create a secret API token under API & Integrations in Apify Console, optionally limiting the token's permission scope and setting an expiration. Organization-level tokens are visible only to owners or members with Manage access tokens permission.
access_notes.quote: To access the Apify API in your integrations, you need to authenticate using your secret API token. You manage your tokens on the API & Integrations page in Apify Console.

official_mcp_server.quote: The Apify's MCP server (mcp.apify.com) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

webhooks.quote: You can configure webhooks to trigger actions based on specific events that occur during Actor runs or builds.

sdk_languages.quote: For Java, we recommend the `apify-client` Maven central component. - For Rust, we recommend the `apify-client` crate. - For .NET, we recommend the `apify-client` Nuget package. - For PHP, we recommend the `apify-client` Packagist package. - For Go, we recommend the `apify-client` package.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Version is carried in the URL path (/v2), and the API reference identifies itself as version 2. No explicit deprecation/sunset policy was found in the supplied evidence.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The Apify API (version 2) provides programmatic access to the Apify platform.

verdict_reason: Apify exposes a public, broadly documented REST API (v2) with an OpenAPI schema and official clients for JavaScript, Python, Go, PHP, Java, .NET, and Rust. Credentials are self-serve: a free account lets a developer create a scoped API token in Apify Console, and the vendor operates an official MCP server at mcp.apify.com. The only real gate is usage-based billing once free-plan usage is exhausted, which is a commercial rather than an access barrier.
open_questions: REST API rate limits were not found in the supplied evidence; confirm any documented per-endpoint or account-level limits.
No dedicated sandbox/test API environment was documented; confirm whether Apify provides one or whether local Actor development/testing is the only pre-production path.
OAuth2 scopes for the core REST API are not documented; the REST API authenticates with API tokens, while OAuth is used for the hosted MCP server.
Free-plan credit amounts and paid-tier pricing were not captured in the evidence bundle (pricing page text absent).
Deprecation/sunset policy for API v2 was not found in the supplied sources.
No GitHub or MCP-registry checks were run, so community MCP servers could not be verified either way.
